messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 Paging: GeoDNS anomaly detected for service.example.com — asymmetric answers observed between Cloudflare and Route53 in EU regions. Severity: P1 - partial customer impact (errors + high latency). Auto-probe shows split answers.

alex: seeing this too. high 5xx rate for EU-west customers. UI errors + increased tail latency.

priya: how widespread? Which regions/ASNs?

miguel: quick datapoints: we run dig from 3 probes:
```
# dig +short @1.1.1.1 service.example.com A
203.0.113.12
# dig +short @8.8.8.8 service.example.com A
198.51.100.7
# dig +short @54.239.28.85 service.example.com A
203.0.113.12
```
Cloudflare resolvers (1.1.1.1) returning 203.0.113.12, Route53 authoritative path sometimes returning 198.51.100.7. clients in eu-west get mixed answers leading to routing to an overloaded POP (203.0.113.12).

ewa: confirmed from our edge metrics: eu-west-1 -> 203.0.113.12 is saturated (request queueing, 504s). Route53-backed regions see lower load. TTLs are 300s, but propagation mismatch causing oscillation.

alex: initial mitigation idea: reduce weight / remove 203.0.113.12 from GeoDNS for EU while we investigate. can someone run the plan?

priya: +1. We should also lower TTLs on the GeoDNS records to 60s to speed convergence, but lower TTL change may take time depending on caches.

miguel: on it — I'm logged into cloudops. plan: 1) add emergency zero-weight for 203.0.113.12 in our GeoDNS policy for EU 2) update Route53 record to point EU -> 198.51.100.7 only (temporary) 3) file support ticket with Cloudflare explaining asymmetry.

sam: can you paste the CLI commands you'll run? I'll follow and watch for side-effects.

miguel: running: 
```bash
# Route53 change (json change batch)
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123456789 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"service.example.com.","Type":"A","TTL":60,"SetIdentifier":"eu-primary","Weight":0,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"203.0.113.12"}]}}]}'

# then set eu-primary to desired IP 198.51.100.7
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123456789 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"service.example.com.","Type":"A","TTL":60,"SetIdentifier":"eu-primary","Weight":100,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"198.51.100.7"}]}}]}'
```
(note: first call zeroes weight on the bad IP, second sets preferred IP)

cloudops-bot: Deploy plan acknowledged. Creating change request CR-4521 and runbook entry.

alex: while changes propagate we should put traffic fallback at the load balancer: enable origin-fallback to nearest healthy IP and activate circuit-breaker to avoid cascading overload. Priya, can you push LB change?

priya: pushing now. LB command: `redwoodctl lb update service --eu fallback-ip=198.51.100.7 --circuit-breaker=50ms`

ewa: monitoring panels: watch EU 5xx, RTT, queue depth. setting alert to mute pager when auto-mitigation finishes to avoid noise.

miguel: Route53 change submitted, changeId: /change/C0H12345. Cloudflare support ticket opened (INC-9987) with dig traces and timestamps.

sam: getting mixed answers still from external resolvers but rate of 203.0.113.12 responses dropping ~40% after change. good sign.

alex: next step: verify client error rate decreasing and that no other regions receive domino effect. Also confirm origin health for 198.51.100.7.

ewa: origin health is green for 198.51.100.7. EU latency dropping slowly. customers reporting fewer errors in last 8m.

miguel: Cloudflare responded: investigating internal caching tier, possible stale geolocation mapping. They recommend purge zone cache for the name and share their purge request id: CF-PURGE-2231. I requested confirmation when purge completes.

priya: purged cache via API: `curl -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/<zone>/purge_cache" -d '{"files":["https://service.example.com/"]}'` and got success response.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation in progress. Status: partial mitigation (traffic shifted away from bad endpoint). Incident lead: alex.

sam: observations: still seeing occasional TTL-stale answers from some ISP resolvers (cached at edge). Should we keep zero-weight on 203.0.113.12 for another TTL cycle (5m)?

alex: yes keep it zeroed for 10m then re-evaluate. No rollback until Cloudflare confirms fix.

ewa: logging note: customer impact window starts 1758004200, end TBD once all caches refresh. adding to incident timeline.

miguel: creating post-incident task list: confirm geo mapping, validate authoritative responses globally, add synthetic probes for split-answer detection, and add automation to failover weight faster.

priya: I'll follow up with a runbook update and an ops-run to rehearse.

cloudops-bot: CR-4521 completed. Route53 reported INSYNC. Cloudflare purge responded success.

incident-bot: Update: service degradation improved. Recommend keeping incident channel open for 1h of observation.

alex: thanks all. I'll hand off to the overnight oncall: @miguel please take post-incident watch and ping if symptoms reappear.

miguel: taking handoff. leaving notes in runbook and will check dashboards every 10m for next hour.

ewa: adding customer-impact note for postmortem: partial errors in eu-west + elevated latency for 23m.

sam: 👍 will collect dig traces from multiple public resolvers for postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident closed (monitoring) — followup tasks created: T1234 (postmortem), T1235 (split-answer detection), T1236 (GeoDNS automation).
